newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end strong, Banespa soars.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end strong, Banespa soars.

text.p: Brazil stocks seesawed to close firm on heavy buying of top blue-chips, with the preferred shares of troubled Sao Paulo state bank Banespa soaring over 30 percent, brokers said.

Banespa preferred, part of the Bovespa index portfolio, surged 32.69 percent to close at 3.45 reais following reports that an accord that would lead to the end of Central Bank administration of the bank is to be announced soon.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares rose 846 points to 1.29 percent, closing at 66,259 points. Volume was 404 million reais ($392.08 million).
Newspapers earlier this week reported that Banespa would become a federal bank and would have a private manager for a year, giving the government time to decide whether to privatize or liquidate it.
The Banespa deal is expected to be part of a refinancing or renegotiation package for Sao Paulo state's huge debt.

Some analysts also welcomed news that Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) would announce the minimum price of mining giant Vale do Rio Doce, due to be privatized in February, on December 17.
"This was good news after all this talk of mounting opposition to Vale's sale," one trader said. to 21.35 reais.
Benchmark Telebras preferred rose 1.95 percent to 78.40 reais at the close.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred gained 2.96 percent to 139 reais, while power utility Eletrobras rose 1.47 percent to end at 344.99 reais.
